title: Beyond Policy Alignment
narration: We present PL-MPC: closing the planning–learning loop.

title: TD-MPC: planning with a learned world model
narration: TD-MPC plans robot actions using a learned world model. The model predicts action outcomes, while a critic estimates return beyond the planning horizon. The robot executes one action, then replans.
purpose: Introduce learned-model predictive control before discussing the contribution. Define the world model, critic, and policy in plain language.
source: sections/01_introduction.tex; sections/02_preliminaries.tex; original architecture planning row
cue: Use the native planning row without PL-MPC contribution badges. Define the world model, critic, and policy beneath it; finish on execute, learn, and replan.

title: Studied problem: beyond policy alignment
narration: The policy proposes actions. Aligning it with the planner leaves three issues: delayed reward propagation, uncertain terminal values, and differences in episode quality.
purpose: Explain the three unresolved issues before presenting PL-MPC. Connect technical interface names to concrete consequences.
cue: Define policy alignment, then present the three unresolved issues. Episode images and return labels are reserved for the RAD explanation.

title: Closing the planning–learning loop
narration: Our method modifies all three interfaces, retaining the world-model architecture and MPPI optimizer.
purpose: Give a compact answer to the problem using the same visual anchor.
cue: Same overview, now emphasizing Our Solution and the three mechanisms.

title: Related work
narration: Prior methods use one-step targets; we use hybrid multi-step targets.
purpose: Locate the contribution without suggesting that all previous methods only modify the actor.
cue: Compare one-step TD targets with PL-MPC hybrid multi-step targets. BMPC uses model-based one-step targets in its reported setup. Sources and auxiliary-critic details remain in notes; no visible footnotes.

title: PL-MPC architecture
narration: Experience updates the world model, critic, and policy, guiding future plans.
purpose: Show where each signal enters using the original architecture, before zooming in.
cue: Native source-architecture objects. Follow A → B → C/D → A; numbered badges locate the three changes.

title: 1. Hybrid multi-step TD targets (MTD)
narration: In this illustration, one trajectory falls while the other survives. Multi-step targets propagate later rewards sooner, helping the critic sharpen the fall–survival boundary. Model predictions complete targets beyond replay.
purpose: Walk from the recorded fall/survival reward ribbons to the schematic boundary. Explain why faster reward propagation can help distinguish outcomes.
cue: Trace the two trajectories and rewards, then the smaller one-step/three-step boundary plot. The original hybrid-target rows y_0^(3), y_1^(3), y_2^(3) show observed/model reward counts (3,0), (2,1), (1,2). Boundary curves are illustrative, not measured.

title: 2. Adaptive terminal estimates (ATE)
narration: After crossing a hurdle, a planned trajectory may enter a less-visited region. When target critics disagree there, ATE penalizes the online terminal value, reducing reliance on uncertain estimates.
purpose: Motivate terminal-value uncertainty using hurdle crossing, then explain the larger disagreement penalty.
cue: Start with the hurdle images, move to ensemble predictions, and finish at the penalized terminal score. Less-visited states are a motivating example; disagreement is an uncertainty proxy.

title: 3. Return-weighted actor distillation (RAD)
narration: RAD gives stronger imitation weight to higher-return episodes, using realized returns rather than critic estimates. Warmup delays this additional loss, allowing the planner to collect useful trajectories first.
purpose: Explain realized-return weighting through the low/high-return examples and explain why RAD is delayed.
cue: Follow episode return to imitation weight to policy update. Finish on the warmup strip. The warmup is a fixed training delay, not an automatic trajectory-quality test; the backbone actor objective stays active.

title: HumanoidBench: balance-hard
narration: On balance-hard, the best seed reaches fifty point nine percent success, versus zero for the baseline seeds. The planner unlocks full-episode balancing, beyond simply raising mean return.
purpose: Highlight successful full-episode balancing and best-seed success, distinguishing it from higher average return.
source: sections/04_experiments.tex, targeted balance-hard ablation paragraph (best seed 50.9%, baseline seeds 0%); project demos
cue: Best-seed success is the main callout: 50.9% for PL-MPC versus 0% for baseline seeds. TAR mean and SD remain secondary. Selected rollouts are representative, not a frequency estimate.

title: HumanoidBench: hurdle
narration: On hurdle, the best seed reaches fifty-eight percent success, versus zero for the baseline seeds. The planner clears successive obstacles and completes the task—a qualitative change in behavior.
purpose: Highlight successful hurdle task completion and the 58.0% best-seed success, beyond aggregate return improvement.
source: sections/04_experiments.tex, targeted hurdle ablation paragraph (best seed 58.0%, matched baseline seeds 0%); project demos
cue: Best-seed success is the main callout: 58.0% for PL-MPC versus 0% for matched baseline seeds. TAR remains mean and SD across three seeds. Full clips play at 5×.

title: Other HumanoidBench tasks
narration: On other HumanoidBench tasks, performance remains competent, with especially large gains on hard tasks such as balance-hard and hurdle.
purpose: Show competent behavior on other tasks while emphasizing the large gains on the two difficult analysis tasks.
cue: Six complete simultaneous rollouts: run, crawl, balance-simple, pole, slide, sit-hard. Playback 7×. These are examples, not an aggregate comparison.
